words.gloss_range: opening conjunction with both coordination and resumptive force
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not add an independent event; it carries the prior refusal into a voiced demand. Its short onset joins 17:90 to 17:89 while also opening the extended demand sequence that runs through 17:93.

topics.headline: joined continuation and fresh demand scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is both connected to the prior refusal and newly staged as direct confrontation.
topics.reason: The conjunction is locally parsed as coordination or resumption, and the following speech clause supplies the new confrontation scene.

topics.headline: launch of the multi-ayah demand sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this opening is not only an ayah opener; it begins the escalating speech unit through 17:93.
topics.reason: The quoted-complement attachment and CRITICAL sequence rows support reading the particle as the entrance to the extended demand speech.

topics.headline: clipped pickup into speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the transition arriving without a lexical buffer, with a clipped pickup into the speech verb.
topics.reason: The particle is a proclitic-like opening before the speech verb, so the row's audible and visual transition payoff is locally coherent.

words.gloss_range: completed plural speech report introducing a direct quotation
words.root_gloss_range: saying, declaring, voicing a stance, and binding utterance; here public refusal is performed through speech
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) fixes a completed collective speech act before the future refusal is heard. The plural verb makes unbelief public and group-voiced, while the q-w-l field makes the quoted words the performance of rejection. Same-surah recurrence with 17:49, 17:94, and commanded speech elsewhere frames this as defiant human speech inside a larger speech-and-belief argument. Its qaf-stop onset gives the speech launch a firm acoustic edge.

topics.headline: completed plural speech act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal first appears as a completed collective utterance, not as private doubt.
topics.reason: The perfect 3mp form and clausal attachment support a completed group speech report governing the quotation.

topics.headline: speech performs the refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted refusal is not merely reported by speech; the speech itself enacts the rejection.
topics.reason: The q-w-l rows survive because the local quote is the exact channel by which the speakers make unbelief public.

topics.headline: same-surah challenge speech pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 17:90 joining the repeated disbeliever-speech pattern of 17:49 and 17:94.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references, and no local grammar blocks the echo.

topics.headline: firm acoustic launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving immediately from connector to a firm speech launch.
topics.reason: The sound and sequence rows describe a local effect tied to the word's opening position.

words.gloss_range: emphatic future negator governing the following subjunctive verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: subjunctive belief verb governed by the negator

words.prose: {{ar:لَن}} ({{tr:lan}}) puts emphatic future negation before any proof is named. It governs {{ar:نُّؤْمِنَ}} ({{tr:nu'mina}}), making the refusal grammatically primary; the later condition therefore reads as a strategy of defiance, not neutral inquiry. Its formula returns in 17:93, bracketing the escalating demands, and the adjacent n-sounds make the negator cling audibly to the belief verb.

topics.headline: emphatic future refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a strong future-facing refusal without needing to overstate the particle as metaphysical eternity.
topics.reason: The local grammar gives emphatic future negation, while the CRITICAL semantic row itself cautions against requiring eternal scope.

topics.headline: negation binds to the belief verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the particle's force in the dependent mood of the belief verb.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment evidence agree that the particle governs the following verb.

topics.headline: refusal precedes the demanded proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the stance is declared before the condition, so the proof demand is secondary to defiance.
topics.reason: The word order and clause structure place the negation before the terminal condition.

topics.headline: refusal formula returns in 17:93
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the refusal formula recurring in 17:93, so the demand sequence is bracketed by the same negated stance.
topics.reason: The echo rows supply the concrete reference 17:93 and fit the extended quotation architecture.

topics.headline: nasal bind into belief verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the negation clinging audibly to the belief verb as narration becomes self-voiced defiance.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is tied to the local particle-verb sequence, and the boundary row fits the quoted-speech shift.

words.gloss_range: negated Form IV first-person plural belief/trust verb aimed through a following lām complement
words.root_gloss_range: security, safety, trust, reliability, and belief; here personal trust in the addressee is the selected force

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: lām complement marking the addressee as trust target
emphatic negator governing the belief verb

words.prose: {{ar:نُّؤْمِنَ}} ({{tr:nu'mina}}) is a first-person plural Form IV verb subordinated under {{ar:لَن}} ({{tr:lan}}), so the group refuses a future act of belief and then pivots toward a demanded geological act. With {{ar:لَكَ}} ({{tr:laka}}), the refusal is not only about content; it targets the addressee as one whose word they will not trust. The ʾ-m-n security field makes that personal refusal a refusal to enter a relation of safety and reliability, and the medial hamza gives the trust verb an audible catch. In 17:94, speech itself is named as the barrier that 17:90 performs.

topics.headline: future belief act grammatically refused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the completed speech report set against a future act of belief that is grammatically blocked.
topics.reason: The verb is the subjunctive complement of the preceding negator and carries first-person plural subject agreement.

topics.headline: lām makes belief personal trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal is aimed at the addressee's credibility, not merely at accepting a proposition.
topics.reason: The lām complement after the belief verb is syntactically forced and supports the trust-target reading.

topics.headline: security field behind trust refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices belief as a security and reliability relation, while local syntax keeps personal trust as the active sense.
topics.reason: The broader root field survives as pressure, but the local lām construction narrows it to trusting the addressee's word.

topics.headline: collective volitional trust act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speakers binding themselves together around a volitional trust act, while causative nuance remains subordinate to the local trust construction.
topics.reason: Form IV and first-person plural are real formal cues, but the local verb means believe or trust rather than requiring a separate causative translation.

topics.headline: speech becomes belief barrier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 17:90 performing the speech-barrier to belief that 17:94 later explains.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete same-surah references and the local quote makes the relation visible.

topics.headline: stance pivots toward demanded action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from self-voiced belief refusal into a demanded geological act.
topics.reason: The verb belongs to the first major clause and is followed by the terminal demand clause.

topics.headline: catch inside the trust verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible catch inside the very verb of trust.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is local to the surface form and carries a modest reader-facing cue.

words.gloss_range: lām plus second-person suffix marking the addressee as the trust target

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: lām plus first-person plural suffix marking the speakers as beneficiaries

words.prose: {{ar:لَكَ}} ({{tr:laka}}) makes the refusal personal: the speakers will not place trust toward this addressee. The compact preposition-pronoun form fixes him as the credibility target, and its later mirror {{ar:لَنَا}} ({{tr:lanā}}) exposes the transaction they propose: trust toward you only if benefit comes for us.

topics.headline: specific addressee as trust target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal is aimed at a specific addressee's credibility.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the phrase the complement of the belief verb, and the second-person suffix fixes the target.

topics.headline: direction toward him, not generic belief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices belief directed toward the addressee, while the local construction keeps benefit language secondary.
topics.reason: The lām can carry direction and benefit, but here the governing belief verb selects personal trust direction as the active force.

topics.headline: trust-target and beneficiary mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exchange structure: trust is withheld from you unless a sign is produced for us.
topics.reason: The later matching lām-pronoun phrase is syntactically present and gives the contrast a local formal basis.

words.gloss_range: terminal or purposive subordinator opening the condition clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: emphatic negator that precedes the condition

words.prose: {{ar:حَتَّىٰ}} ({{tr:ḥattā}}) is the hinge between refusal and demand. Its scope runs through the final spring object, so the whole earth-spring clause is the claimed endpoint of unbelief. Because {{ar:لَن}} ({{tr:lan}}) already made refusal emphatic, this endpoint functions as a challenge condition, and 17:91 continues the escalation it opens.

topics.headline: condition scope reaches the final object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle governs the whole demanded miracle clause, not only the next verb.
topics.reason: The attachment constraints identify the complete following phrase as the purpose or limit clause.

topics.headline: claimed endpoint turned challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a conditional shape being used as a challenge after emphatic refusal has already been voiced.
topics.reason: The condition is grammatically real, while the preceding emphatic negation narrows it away from neutral inquiry.

topics.headline: hinge between negated belief and demanded act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's two-part architecture: stance first, demanded action second.
topics.reason: The particle sits between the belief verb and the demanded action verb and governs the latter's dependent form.

topics.headline: compact hinge opens escalation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compact pivot opening a forward slot that the following ayahs expand.
topics.reason: The form and boundary rows describe a local hinge that is confirmed by the forward demand sequence.

words.gloss_range: second-person Form I subjunctive verb demanding direct splitting or bursting open
words.root_gloss_range: splitting, cleaving, bursting forth, dawn break, and boundary breach; here physical earth-rupture for water release is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: subordinating particle that governs the demanded action

words.prose: {{ar:تَفْجُرَ}} ({{tr:tafjura}}) is the demanded action word: a second-person subjunctive under {{ar:حَتَّىٰ}} ({{tr:ḥattā}}), aimed at the addressee and filled out by beneficiary, source, and object. The f-j-r field gives physical rupture and release, locally narrowed to splitting the earth for a spring. Form I makes the canonical demand direct, while the Form II variant and other causative pressures show the same slot testing agency; 17:37 has already marked earth-tearing as beyond the addressee, and 17:91 immediately intensifies the f-j-r demand. The same root has marked sacred time at 17:78, so the local hydraulic rupture is heard against a distinct same-surah domain. Its compact stop-and-release texture suits a marked rupture verb before the longer specifying chain.

topics.headline: beneficiary source and object gathered by the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demanded act specified as for us, from earth, a spring, rather than a bare miracle verb.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence forces the beneficiary, source phrase, and direct object as dependents of the verb.

topics.headline: subordinate second-person demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a future performance aimed directly at the addressee but embedded inside their condition.
topics.reason: The verb is second-person singular and subjunctive under the preceding particle, with the subject morphologically present.

topics.headline: earth rupture releasing hidden water
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the concrete image of a sealed surface being breached so hidden water can emerge, while moral and dawn branches stay secondary.
topics.reason: The local source phrase and spring object select the water-release branch, narrowing broader f-j-r domains.

topics.headline: direct Form I with causative variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical form casts the addressee as direct splitter, while variant evidence exposes a real agency pressure around causing the gushing.
topics.reason: Accepted variant evidence may illuminate the agency contrast, but the local canonical parse remains Form I.

topics.headline: impossible earth-rupture demand escalates
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand pressing against 17:37's denied earth-tearing and then intensifying in 17:91.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows provide concrete references and fit the local earth-rupture demand.

topics.headline: f-j-r root moves across domains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same root moving from the sacred time-marker of 17:78 to the demanded spring rupture of 17:90, while the local sense remains hydraulic rupture.
topics.reason: The same-surah echo is concrete, but it must not replace the locally selected water-release sense.

topics.headline: abrupt rare rupture word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a compact, marked rupture verb that releases into the longer demand chain.
topics.reason: The constrained distribution and local sound observations are modest but coherent reader-facing payoffs.

words.gloss_range: benefactive lām plus first-person plural suffix under the demanded action verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: lām plus second-person suffix marking the addressee as trust target

words.prose: {{ar:لَنَا}} ({{tr:lanā}}) makes the speakers the beneficiaries before the source phrase arrives. The same group that says we will not believe now says the spring must be for us, turning evidence into entitlement. Its mirror with {{ar:لَكَ}} ({{tr:laka}}) structures the exchange: trust toward you in return for benefit for us.

topics.headline: speakers as demanded beneficiaries
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demanded sign must serve the speakers, not simply occur as proof.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the phrase the benefactive complement of the demanded action verb.

topics.headline: beneficiary named before source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand foregrounding who benefits before naming where the spring emerges.
topics.reason: The local order places the benefactive phrase immediately after the verb and before the source phrase.

topics.headline: we as subject and beneficiary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speakers moving from refusing subject to demanded beneficiary through repeated first-person plural marking.
topics.reason: The suffix mirrors the earlier first-person plural verb and the earlier lām-pronoun phrase.

words.gloss_range: source preposition governing the earth phrase
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) turns the demanded sign toward origin: the spring must come from the earth, not merely appear near it. It governs the definite earth phrase and bridges the clause from beneficiary to source before the delayed object arrives, with the nasal source particle binding audibly into that earth phrase. That source framing starts the below-ground side of the vertical demand axis later answered by sky-demand language in 17:92.

topics.headline: source preposition from the earth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices origin from the earth, while partitive extraction is not the active local sense.
topics.reason: The source phrase is governed by the preposition and selected by the bursting verb plus earth noun.

topics.headline: earth phrase governed as source complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand being grammatically routed through the ground as source.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following earth noun as the prepositional complement.

topics.headline: origin named before result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the origin image building before the spring itself is named.
topics.reason: The local order places the source phrase before the direct object.

topics.headline: below-source axis and audible binding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition anchoring the below-ground pole of the demand sequence and binding audibly into the earth phrase.
topics.reason: The vertical-axis row gives concrete reference to 17:92, and the sound row is local to the source phrase.

topics.headline: hiddenness routed into emergence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the refused or concealed truth mirrored by a demand that what is hidden below ground become visible.
topics.reason: The boundary row is interpretive but anchored in the local source-emergence construction.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive earth or ground as the demanded source
words.root_gloss_range: earth, ground, land, lower surface, and substrate; here the physical ground is selected as sealed source-domain
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضِ}} ({{tr:al-arḍi}}) completes the source phrase as a definite genitive singular noun, so the demand points to the known ground as one source-domain for the spring. The broader arḍ range is narrowed to physical substrate, but its lower-surface pressure remains: the earth is the sealed layer they demand opened, and the source phrase is heard as a unit before the final spring resolves it. This recalls 17:37, where earth-tearing was denied to the addressee, begins the lower pole of the earth-to-sky escalation that reaches 17:92, and recasts the earth-spring pairing of 39:21 as a demand placed on the addressee.

topics.headline: genitive source complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the earth functioning as source complement, not as independent subject or object.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the noun in the source phrase attached to the demanded action verb.

topics.headline: known ground as sealed source-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand targeting the definite ground beneath the scene as a sealed source, while broader land meanings remain secondary.
topics.reason: The source preposition and spring object narrow the root range to physical ground or substrate.

topics.headline: definite singular source-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the singular definite form presenting the ground as one unified source-domain.
topics.reason: The noun instance evidence identifies a definite singular concrete noun in a source prepositional phrase.

topics.headline: earth-tearing impossibility reactivated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand pressing against 17:37's denied ability to tear the earth.
topics.reason: The same-surah contrast is concrete and directly concerns earth plus rupture.

topics.headline: lower pole of escalating demands
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first demand beginning below, before the sequence escalates toward sky-demand language in 17:92.
topics.reason: The vertical-axis rows provide concrete forward reference and fit the demand sequence.

topics.headline: earth and springs in divine water-routing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the earth-spring pairing of 39:21 being recast here as a demand placed on the addressee.
topics.reason: The cross-reference is concrete and preserves the contrast between divine water-routing and the local demand.

topics.headline: source phrase heard as one unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the source phrase heard as a unit before the final spring resolves it.
topics.reason: The sound and order rows are local to the prepositional phrase and its position before the object.

topics.headline: speech contrast belongs elsewhere
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The row mainly discusses q-w-l speech contrast with 17:28 and adds no distinct local payoff for the earth noun beyond retained speech and demand-sequence topics.
topics.reason: The concrete reference is not false, but its reader-facing value is about speech roles rather than this word's earth-source function.

words.gloss_range: singular indefinite accusative object naming a spring or welling source
words.root_gloss_range: springing forth, emerging, becoming apparent, and a source of outflow; here a concrete spring-source is demanded into visibility
words.prose: {{ar:يَنۢبُوعًا}} ({{tr:yanbūʿan}}) is the final object of the demand: singular, indefinite, accusative, and unqualified. It completes the rupture frame as spring-production, not mere splitting. The n-b-ʿ field makes the object a source of hidden emergence, while its rarity and contrast with the plural springs of 39:21 sharpen the mismatch between one demanded spring here and divine water-routing elsewhere. As the sentence-final word, its tanwīn gives nasal indefinite closure and lands the whole ayah on an unspecified source demanded into visibility, a single spring that 17:91 expands into a broader water-landscape demand.

topics.headline: unspecified accusative object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand ending in one concrete but unspecified object: a spring.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as the direct object and lacks the definite article.

topics.headline: spring-production completes the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested sign is not just splitting but producing a spring as result object.
topics.reason: The object is governed by the verb rather than by the source preposition.

topics.headline: hidden source emerging into visibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a spring as a point of concealed supply becoming visible, while the local noun remains a concrete water source.
topics.reason: The broader emergence field survives because it is realized in the concrete spring noun and source phrase.

topics.headline: place or instrument of emergence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the word naming a source-function, not merely water as substance.
topics.reason: The supplied pattern analysis coheres with the noun's role as a spring-source.

topics.headline: sentence-final indefinite closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word completing the grammar while keeping the demanded spring unspecified.
topics.reason: The word's final position and tanwīn both support the closure and indefiniteness payoff.

topics.headline: one demanded spring against 39:21's plural springs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the singular demanded spring here set against the plural divine springs of 39:21.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give a concrete 39:21 comparison and distributional rarity for the singular form.

topics.headline: object delayed after the source phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the source image building before the spring is named at the ayah close.
topics.reason: The local clause order delays the direct object until after the source phrase.

topics.headline: nasal closure and next demand seed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the demand closing on an indefinite sound while the single spring becomes the seed for the broader water-landscape demand in 17:91.
topics.reason: The sound row is local to the final word, and the forward boundary row has the concrete next-ayah continuation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَقَالُوا لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ ... لَنَا
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers turn assent into a negotiated exchange: they reserve trust until the addressee performs a beneficiary-specific deliverable.

activation_trace.role: The branch image of negotiation makes their utterance function as terms proposed in a bargain.
Heart-settling assent is explicitly withheld as the consideration to be exchanged.

changed_reading.before: They simply announce that they do not yet believe.
changed_reading.after: They frame belief as payment conditional on satisfying terms they control.

baseline_models.mechanism: A wide breach is to open the lower ground so a hidden source becomes sustained visible outflow; the demanded sign is engineered disclosure rather than a momentary anomaly.

activation_trace.role: Wide splitting and emission supplies the breach that releases the demanded water.
The lower realm opposite the sky supplies the material layer to be opened.
Water emerging from an eye or the earth supplies the continuing visible source.

changed_reading.before: They ask for a miraculous spring.
changed_reading.after: They demand that concealed provision be forced through the earth into an inspectable, continuing source.

baseline_models.mechanism: The requested proof must not only certify a claim but also become a usable resource for the speakers; credibility is tied to material security delivered for us.

activation_trace.role: Security and trust make belief carry an affective demand for settled safety.
A real water source gives the requested security a durable material form.

changed_reading.before: The spring serves only as evidence for a proposition.
changed_reading.after: The sign must also secure the speakers materially, making trust depend on a resource delivered for their benefit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The root used for forced water-bursting also names dawn, whose recitation is witnessed. The demand shifts verification from a recurrent opening in time and recitation to a customized rupture in matter.

activation_trace.role: The focus uses wide splitting and emission as the requested hydraulic performance.
Dawn supplies a recurrent opening out of night rather than a requester-engineered rupture.
Presence with observation supplies the context's explicit mode of witnessing.

structural_cues: 17:78 repeats ف ج ر around the recitation and predicates witnessed presence of it, while 17:90 uses حَتَّىٰ to impose a different evidentiary threshold.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared ف ج ر root and explicit witnessing; I infer a contrast between given recurrent disclosure and commissioned spectacle. A live alternative is that dawn and water are merely separate senses with no polemical contrast.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, varied exempla, and persisting refusal; I infer that the spring is a replacement criterion in a moving test. A live alternative is that it specifies a genuinely unmet category of evidence.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated earth, the human objection, and the inhabitant-messenger counterfactual; I infer a medium-mismatch behind the requested sign. A live alternative is that the demands challenge authority without rejecting embodiment itself.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because ف ج ر B005 is a generosity branch rather than the immediate hydraulic sense. It remains anchored in the focus verb, لَنَا, and the nearby bounty and garden-river sequence; downstream prose should present it as branch-play that supplements, not replaces, the water sense.

activation_trace.role: Wide bursting generosity lets the requested act be heard as compelled largesse for the speakers.
Benefaction and gift supply a nearby model of bounty that is given rather than commissioned.
The river demand expands the imagined largesse from one source into an entire productive estate.

changed_reading.before: The spectacle is requested only to certify the messenger.
changed_reading.after: The demand also tries to conscript prophetic agency into producing distributable bounty for the requester group.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because ن ب ع B004 transfers a speech image onto the noun for a water source. It remains focus-only and anchored by the opening قَالُوا and closing يَنۢبُوعًا; downstream prose should mark it as a verbal-material echo, not the noun's primary contextual sense.

activation_trace.role: Audible utterance supplies the speakers' emergence into voiced demand.

changed_reading.before: Their utterance merely names the spring they want.
changed_reading.after: Their own voiced demand becomes a speech-spring, verbally enacting the emergence they require from the earth.

strongest_changes: The spring condition becomes a negotiated and recursively movable proof regime rather than a finite test.
The witnessed dawn and recipient-dependent recitation expose disclosure and reception already operating outside requester control.
The earth demand is sharpened by the later rejection of a human messenger proportioned to earthly recipients.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly reuses focus roots across different media: ف ج ر joins dawn to water, ء م ن tracks changing reception and repeated refusal, and ء ر ض joins the demanded site to the messenger-recipient fit.
remaining_uncertainties: The dawn-water contrast may be deliberate activation or only polysemy within the shared root.
The escalation can indicate moving goalposts, but it can also be read as a cumulative catalog of desired signs.
The generosity and speech-spring readings are branch-distant and should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Assent is made conditional on controllable terrestrial outflow.** `ء م ن:B002` trusting assent, `ف ج ر:B001` wide splitting/outflow, `ء ر ض:B001/B002` lower fertile ground, and `ن ب ع:B001/B004` springing water or bursting speech. The demanded sign must split ground “for us.” I infer they replace trust with patron-controlled production. The spring reads as a test not of truth but of whether the messenger can be made to furnish desired infrastructure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:99's invitation to see creation answers the demand from ordinary perception, while 17:101's nine signs shows that even extraordinary visibility can be covered. The requested spring is therefore a movable condition, not a stable test.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Belief is recast as payment after controlled spectacle.** Lexical evidence: `ء م ن B002` (trusting assent and confirmation) in `نُّؤْمِنَ`, `ف ج ر B001` (wide splitting and outflow) in `تَفْجُرَ`, and `ن ب ع B001` (water springing from a source) in `يَنۢبُوعًا`. Structural cue: 17:88–89 presents an unreproducible yet widely varied Qur'an; `حَتَّىٰ` now makes assent conditional on a spring produced `لَنَا`, and 17:91–93 escalates the demanded control over garden, sky, ascent, and book. Assigned role: earth-splitting creates visible outflow, while the beneficiary phrase turns the sign into a negotiated service. Abductive move: the condition is supplied; I infer that the speakers seek control over evidence-production rather than clarification of existing evidence. Reading change: unbelief adopts a transactional posture: trust will be released only after the messenger performs a materially useful spectacle on demand.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:91–93 escalated the condition from useful spring to total vertical control, and 17:95 answered with messenger ecology; together they confirmed that the demand was governance of proof, not missing evidence.

Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek bir haberin, sozun veya hakikatin dogru sayilmasidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, çok sayıda insanın ya da belanın bir topluluğun üzerine ansızın gelmesini açıkça kurar. Miktar, beklenmedik geliş ve etkilenen topluluk birlikte korunması gereken anlam bileşenleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız belirtilen üzerine gelme kuruluşuna bağlıdır; bu anlam tek başına genel bir gelme ya da patlama anlamına genişletilmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, doğruluktan sapıp kötülüklere açılmayı; yalanı, başkaldırıyı, inancı reddetmeyi ve cinsel sınır çiğnemeyi bunun görünümleri olarak destekler. Geçici çerçevedeki fiziksel yana yatma ise dalın kurucu ahlaki anlamı değil, ayrı bir söz öbeğinde görülen sınırlı bir uzantıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dalın çekirdeği ahlaki ve inançsal sınırları çiğnemektir; fiziksel eğrilik yalnız ilgili söz öbeğinin ayrı sözlüksel karşılığında kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım ahlaki sapma çekirdeğini verir; yalan, başkaldırı ve benzeri kullanımlar ile fiziksel eğiklik bildiren söz öbeği birbirine karıştırılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Doğruluk ve inanç sınırlarını yarıp kötülüklere yönelmek, böylece doğru yoldan belirgin biçimde sapmaktır. Yalan, taşkın kötülük, başkaldırı, inancı reddetme ve cinsel sınır çiğneme bunun özel görünümleridir.

facets.statement: Kişi doğruluk ve inanç sınırlarını çiğneyerek doğru yoldan sapar.
Yalan söylemek, kötülüklere dalmak, başkaldırmak, inancı reddetmek ve cinsel sınırı çiğnemek bu sapmanın özel görünümleridir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar doğruluktan sapma ve inanç sınırını çiğneme çekirdeğinde birleşir; yalan, kötülüklere dalma, başkaldırı, inancı reddetme ve cinsel yanlış bu geniş sapmanın belirtilen görünümleridir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalan ve başkaldırı gibi özel eylemlerin bağlı olduğu geniş ahlaki sapma çekirdeği kastedildiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Doğru yoldan ayrılmayı, sınır çiğnemeyi ve kötülüğe yönelmeyi birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin geniş ve belirgin ahlaki sapmasını doğal bir yüklemle anlatmak için kullanılır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal fiziksel su akışını ya da ahlaki sapmayı değil, iyilik ve vermedeki geniş bolluğu anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım eli açıklık çekirdeğini verir; kişinin iyiliğinin bolluğu ve çokça varlık getirmesi yalnız belirtilen yapılara bağlı özelleşmelerdir.
